review_notes: I read the whole file. It has no @[simp] attributes. The simp-relevant pieces are the apply-style lemmas for the new defs kwTrivLift and kwKerAlg, which are not abbrevs and so are opaque to simp. I looked at all uses of kw_rglcktf_trivLift_apply and kw_rglcktfm_kerAlg_apply in the file. I did not check other files for uses, and I could not run Lean, so I make no claim about observed simp behaviour. I looked for competing rules or loops and found none, since nothing is tagged simp. kwTensorPair is an abbrev, so its unfolding works via `simp only [kwTensorPair, ...]`. I did not flag the other rfl-style lemmas (schemeHomOverComp_idPoint, nsmul_coe_eq_comp_schemeNsmul) because they are used once each and their LHS shapes are not obviously canonical. The kerAlg_apply finding is lower confidence because its uses mix both rewrite directions.

findings.excerpt:
theorem kw_rglcktf_trivLift_apply (x : B) :
    kwTrivLift ε₀ x = algebraMap R R' (ε₀ x) := by
findings.problem: kwTrivLift is a plain `def`, so simp cannot see through it. The coercion lemma `kwTrivLift ε₀ x = algebraMap R R' (ε₀ x)` is the only way to expose its meaning, and it is proved by `rfl`. It is not tagged @[simp]. Every use has to name it by hand: `rw [kw_rglcktf_trivLift_apply]` at lines 147, 176, 265, 268 and 507, and in the explicit `simp only` list at line 284. The same file uses `simp [RingHom.mem_ker, map_sub, AlgHom.commutes]` at line 163, where the default simp set would not be able to unfold kwTrivLift if it appeared. That makes the normal form unclear. The definition's meaning depends on callers remembering a lemma name.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the lemma `@[simp]`. Its LHS is a head symbol applied to arguments with a fixed shape, and the RHS is built from `algebraMap` and `ε₀` only, so it cannot loop. Then drop the explicit `rw [kw_rglcktf_trivLift_apply]` calls and the entry in the `simp only` list at line 284 where plain `simp` or `simp only [...]` suffices. As an alternative, add `@[simp]` to a `kwTrivLift_apply` lemma and keep the current name as a deprecated alias.
findings.benefit: The normal form for kwTrivLift applications is a single `algebraMap R R' (ε₀ x)`. This removes manual rewrite bookkeeping in the four-term and tensor-pair arguments. It also stops simp calls such as line 163 from getting stuck on an opaque `kwTrivLift ε₀ x` that is not already unfolded.

findings.excerpt:
theorem kw_rglcktfm_kerAlg_apply (k : SchemeHomOver t f) (hk : KwIsKerElt G φ t k)
    (b : B₁) :
    kwKerAlg G B₁ ι hιf hιe φ hsurj hker t htR' k hk b
      = (kwKerRing G B₁ ι hιe φ hsurj hker t k hk).hom b
findings.problem: kwKerAlg is a `def` wrapping the ring hom `(kwKerRing ...).hom` with a proof of `commutes'`. The underlying-function lemma is this one, proved by `rfl`, and it is not a simp lemma. Because it is used in both directions, the file has no stable normal form. Forward `rw` appears at lines 507, 567 and 622. Reverse `rw [← ...]` appears at lines 568 and 728–729, where the lemma has to be restated with all its arguments to re-fold. A further congruence lemma, `kw_rglcktfm_kerAlg_val_eq`, is needed only to move between `kwKerAlg` terms with different proofs `hk`. Its proof is `subst h; rfl`.
findings.proposed_change: Choose one normal form. Make `kw_rglcktfm_kerAlg_apply` `@[simp]` so that `kwKerAlg ... k hk b` reduces to the `kwKerRing` hom application. The two reverse rewrites at lines 568 and 728–729 would then become unnecessary if the goals are stated in terms of `kwKerRing`, or they can be handled by `simp`/`simp only [kw_rglcktfm_kerAlg_apply]` on both sides. Since `hk` is a Prop proof argument, the proof-irrelevant instances of the simp lemma will match without a separate `_val_eq` lemma.
findings.benefit: Calls such as `rw [← lemma G B₁ ι hιf hιe φ hsurj hker t htR', ← lemma ...]` (line 728) would shrink to a single simp call. The statements of `kw_rglcktfm_kerAlg_reduces` and `kw_rglcktfm_kerAlg_mul_fourTerm` could be reasoned about uniformly in terms of the underlying ring hom.
